D.t: JB Pritzker leads by 25.1 in the forecast and wins 100% of simulations. The cushion is about 1,165,818 votes; a one point swing is about 23,251 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +17.8 and D +32.6. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The polls page average is D +20.0. Your best recent poll is Public Policy Polling for Chicago News Weekly at D +20.4; your worst is ActiVote at D +17.4. 2 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Cook, a projected net 1,032,798 votes; DuPage, a projected net 117,357 votes; Lake, a projected net 89,653 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: McHenry, D +10.3, 2.7% of the vote; Madison, R +0.3, 2.3% of the vote; Winnebago, D +9.2, 2.1% of the vote; Sangamon, D +4.8, 1.8% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, JB Pritzker runs furthest behind in McLean, Champaign, Winnebago. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 76% of voters, 55 to 42, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.77 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 64% of voters, 61 to 36, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.18 points; Voters without a degree, 58% of voters, 56 to 41, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.89 points.
The forecast's worst groups for JB Pritzker: Immigration voters 26 to 71, Small counties 33 to 63, Midsize counties 51 to 45. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$44.4M cash against $482K. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.
